summary.business_type: B2B Technology Services & Software Consultancy (Programmatic local service pages)
summary.audit_method: Full crawl of all 473 sitemap URLs via simulated browser session (JS-challenge pass-through), per-page on-page parsing, UA-specific crawler-access probes for Googlebot, Bingbot, GPTBot, DuckDuckBot, YandexBot, Applebot

top_findings.title: Hosting anti-bot JS challenge blocks every crawler except Googlebot/Bingbot
379 of 473 page titles exceed 60 characters (programmatic template)
/blog is indexed in the sitemap but contains zero posts (renders 'No posts yet')
Near-identical templated copy across 460 programmatic service×city pages

quick_wins: Shorten title template for 460 geo pages: drop 'Best' and 'Company', or move brand out of the pattern (e.g. 'Mobile App Development in Lucknow — Ecotech Services')
Trim 216 geo-page meta descriptions to ≤155 characters by cutting the second sentence
Populate the /blog with at least one real post or remove /blog from the sitemap until it has content
Add 301 redirects: http:// → https:// and www → non-www (canonical tags currently mask duplicate hosts)
After hosting fix, resubmit all 473 URLs via IndexNow and verify AI-crawler access to /llms.txt

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: All 473 sitemap URLs return HTTP 200 in a full crawl (0 errors, 0 redirects-in-sitemap)
HSTS now live: Strict-Transport-Security max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload (previous audit finding fixed)
Full security header set: X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy, X-XSS-Protection
Gzip compression confirmed working (42KB page → 7KB wire size)
True 404 status codes for nonexistent URLs (no soft-404s)
Googlebot (3/3 probes) and Bingbot (1/1) receive full 40.5KB pages, no challenge
Self-referencing canonicals correct on all 473 pages; no robots-meta noindex anywhere

findings.title: JS anti-bot challenge wall serves crawlers a 847-891-byte stub
findings.description: Live host is InfinityFree free shared hosting (IP 185.27.134.149, Server: openresty). First-time cookie-less sessions receive a JavaScript cookie challenge (aes.js / __test). Probes: GPTBot 3/3 challenge-page, DuckDuckBot challenge, Applebot challenge, YandexBot HTTP 403; with a desktop-browser UA, 5/5 initial requests dropped the TLS connection entirely (curl 56, missing close_notify) and the rest returned the challenge stub. Content is only reachable after executing JS and carrying the __test cookie. This also explains the 'SSL handshake abrupt termination' flagged in the 2026-10-26 audit — the root cause is the hosting layer, not the certificate (Let's Encrypt chain verified valid).
findings.recommendation: Move to paid hosting (the codebase already targets Hostinger SMTP; a basic Hostinger/shared paid plan removes the challenge layer entirely). Alternative minimum mitigation: any CDN/proxy in front that serves content without the challenge. After migration, verify with GSC URL Inspection and re-probe all six crawler UAs.

findings.title: AI search engines receive the challenge and cannot index anything — including /llms.txt and /sitemap.xml
findings.description: robots.txt explicitly allows GPTBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot, Applebot-Extended, and /llms.txt (2.8KB, well-structured) is published — but YandexBot gets 403, GPTBot/DuckDuckBot/Applebot get the JS challenge on every path tested, including static text files. AI crawlers do not execute JavaScript, so llms.txt is currently unreachable server-side despite returning 200 with correct content to humans.
findings.recommendation: Fixed automatically by the hosting migration; verify afterwards by probing /llms.txt with GPTBot/PerplexityBot UAs. Until then AI Search Readiness is effectively zero despite compliant robots.txt.

findings.title: No 301 redirects for http:// and www host variants
findings.description: http://ecotechservices.tech and https://www.ecotechservices.tech return 200 directly (no redirect to the canonical host). Self-canonical tags mitigate duplicate-host indexing, but link equity across host variants is split and any canonical-tag parsing error creates genuine duplicates.
findings.recommendation: Add 301 redirects for both variants at the web root after migration (InfinityFree htdocs .htaccess supports RewriteRule).

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy header
findings.description: All other security headers are present; CSP is the missing one. Not a ranking factor but a security and Page-Experience hygiene item.
findings.recommendation: Add (e.g.) 'Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; cdnjs.allow' tuned to the existing cdnjs.cloudflare.com dependencies.

findings.title: /blog indexed in sitemap, zero posts
findings.description: /blog (178 words) renders the heading 'No posts yet'. No /blog/post URLs exist in the sitemap. An empty indexed section signals site neglect to both users and quality raters and wastes crawl budget.
findings.recommendation: Either publish a starter batch (3-5 posts reusing existing geo-page research topics) and only then keep /blog in the sitemap, or drop /blog from the sitemap and noindex it until real posts exist.

findings.title: Templated copy across 460 service×city pages
findings.description: The 460/473 programmatic pages (23 service types × up-to-36-city grid) share near-identical copy — e.g. 'We provide [Service] for businesses in [City] — fast, scalable and secure solutions built around how your business actually works.' — with only the entity swap. Google's scaled-content-abuse guidance explicitly targets search-first-generated pages created to manipulate rankings; average 338 words of interchangeable text is a live risk for the whole grid.
findings.recommendation: Differentiate at minimum: per-city intro paragraph referencing a real local project/market fact, 3-4 unique FAQs per city, one local proof point (testimonial, delivered project, or response-time SLA). Prioritise the 36 × primary-service pages, then roll out.

categories.name: On-Page SEO
what_works: Zero duplicate titles and zero duplicate descriptions across all 473 pages
Exactly one H1 per page on all 473 pages
Self-referencing canonical on 473/473 pages, no mismatches
34 images crawled, 0 missing alt attributes
Title/meta present on 100% of pages

findings.title: 379 titles exceed the 60-character truncation limit
findings.description: Distribution: 358/420 'other service' city pages (avg 67.7 chars), 20/20 mobile-app pages (avg 65), 1/20 web-dev pages, 3/7 core pages. Typical offender: 'Best Mobile App Development Company in Bangalore | Ecotech Services' (67 chars → '…| Ecotech Services' is cut in SERPs). Truncation removes the brand and CTA word and gives full SERP control to Google's rewrite.
findings.recommendation: Change the title template to '[Service] in [City] | Ecotech Services' (drops 'Best' and 'Company': Bangalore example 67→48 chars). One-line change in the shared per-service controller.

findings.title: 216 meta descriptions exceed 160 characters
findings.description: 211/420 other-service pages (avg 161.6 chars) plus 4/20 mobile pages plus 1 core page. Google truncates at ~155-160 desktop / ~120 mobile, so the closing sales phrase is consistently severed.
findings.recommendation: Shorten template to ≤155 chars: keep '[Service] for [City] businesses' + one differentiator, delete the second sentence.

findings.title: AggregateRating / Review markup still absent
findings.description: Unchanged from the previous audit: no verified reviews anywhere, so no rich-result stars. Now locally relevant on 460 service pages where review stars would differentiate SERPs.
findings.recommendation: Collect 5-6 verified client reviews, then add AggregateRating + review arrays to the ProfessionalService node with a politeness policy per city page.

findings.title: FAQPage schema absent on programmatic pages
findings.description: If per-city FAQs are added (Content finding), pairing them with FAQPage JSON-LD gives the tiles a second rich-result surface.
findings.recommendation: Add FAQPage JSON-LD alongside the per-city FAQ copy when it ships.

categories.name: Performance (Core Web Vitals)
what_works: Crawl-measured response times: avg 1.55s, p95 2.32s, incl. network + TLS from a single client (no CrUX field data available in this audit)
Gzip active; lean server-rendered HTML (no client framework hydration)
Only 1 CDN dependency (cdnjs.cloudflare.com) per page; minimal third-party JS
Long-cache static assets noted in previous audit remain in place

findings.title: First-hit UX penalty from anti-bot challenge, outliers above 16s
findings.description: A real first-time visitor's first request frequently returns the JS interstitial plus an extra redirect (?i=1), which delays LCP and consumes a hop before content; single worst observed crawl time 16.3s. Field CWV (CrUX) could not be measured in this audit.
findings.recommendation: Resolves with the hosting migration; after migration, measure LCP/INP/CLS in CrUX via GSC for the 7 core pages first, then template pages.

robots.txt explicitly allows GPTBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot, Applebot-Extended
Server-rendered HTML rewards anything that does get in: no JS needed to read content
IndexNow key file live at /82568927e2e0467eac3f26e8e621ea0a.txt

findings.title: AI crawlers receive the JS challenge on 100% of tested paths
findings.description: GPTBot: challenge page on /, /llms.txt, /sitemap.xml, service pages (3/3 and 4/4). DuckDuckBot, Applebot: challenge. YandexBot: HTTP 403. AI answers therefore cannot cite this site even though robots.txt welcomes the same bots — the allow rules are dead letters at the application layer.
findings.recommendation: Host migration (see Technical SEO). After migration, probe / and /llms.txt with GPTBot/PerplexityBot/ClaudeBot UAs and confirm 200 + real content, then resubmit via IndexNow.

findings.title: Third-party screenshot service (image.thum.io) referenced
findings.description: A blog/portfolio link points to image.thum.io, an external thumbnail-rendering service — an availability and latency dependency for visual content.
findings.recommendation: Render portfolio thumbnails to local WebP/AVIF files instead of calling the third-party thumbnail service at view time.

phases.name: Phase 1: Crawl Availability & Template Fixes
items: Migrate off InfinityFree to paid shared hosting (Hostinger base plan) — removes the JS challenge for every crawler at once (Critical)
Verify post-migration: GSC URL Inspection on /, plus UA probes for GPTBot, PerplexityBot, DuckDuckBot, YandexBot on / and /llms.txt
One-line title template fix on 460 geo pages: '[Service] in [City] | Ecotech Services' (fixes 379 truncated titles)

phases.name: Phase 2: Programmatic Pages & Indexing
items: Add per-city uniqueness to the 36 primary-service pages: unique intro, 3 FAQs (with FAQPage schema), one local proof point; then roll the pattern to the 20-city secondary services
Decide /blog: publish 3-5 posts or noindex it and drop from sitemap until populated
Add 301 redirects http→https and www→apex; resubmit sitemap + all 473 URLs via submitIndexNow()

phases.name: Phase 3: Authority & Rich Results
items: Collect verified client reviews; add AggregateRating/Review to ProfessionalService
Cover-ship the /internships page into the sitemap (live but unlisted; it has inbound portfolio/footer links)

Measure CrUX CWV in GSC for core pages; fix whatever misses thresholds

phases.name: Phase 4: Monitoring
items: Monthly re-crawl of the 473-URL sitemap with per-UA crawler probes (rerun this audit)
AI-citation spot checks: ask ChatGPT/Perplexity 'best [service] in [city]' for the 36 priority pages
Watch GSC coverage for the service×city grid; remove permanently unindexable combos from the sitemap
